main_text.p: & tenuissimâ praeditum substantiâ, & tamen rigidis ac densis Sphæris conflatum esse queat?

Deinde ipsa in cœlo sidera sponte sua conficiunt spatia, Gen. 1. v. 15. Deus sidera in ex-panso cœli collocavit, ut terram circumquaq; il-lustrent, & ratas temporum periodos definiant, 2. Movendi quoq; vim, qua hoc expedire pos-sunt, una iisdem insevit. 3. Ipsa stellæ oriri & occidere dicuntur, properare & circumire, Ec-cl. 1. 3. Luna substitisse narratur, Josu. 10. Ha-bac. 3. Summa, Ortus, occasus, statio, progressio, & reliqua quæ motum præsupponunt, non cœlo, sed stellis tribuuntur. 4. Si reales essent in cœlo orbes, tot essent, quot distincti motus in cœlo reperiuntur. At non hoc: Fixæ enim stellæ duplicem habere motum dicuntur. E. & geminos saltem orbes: Planetæ singuli variis motibus agitari videntur: Varios igitur rotabiles orbes habebunt. 5. Cum stellæ dicuntur densiores partes sui orbis, & clarè cernantur, certè etiam ipsæ duræ & vastæ machinæ præfulgidæ cernentur.
Expansio illa continua in S. literis celebratur, instar pellis, utris, vesicæ, vel Tapetis, Psal. 104. v. 2. Jesa. 40. v.22. & 42. v.5.
Huc accedit Augustin.lib.2.de Gen. ad literam. Ambr.lib.2. Hexam.cap.4. Basil.Homil. 3. Notetur & vox Hebræa, Rakia, expansum.

page.notes: The Tironian "&" symbol is written as &. The catchword is printed "Eft" and is given as Est. The "6," at the foot is read as signature 6; the comma is printed after it. The word "distincti" (printed "distinƈti") is a doubtful ligature and is read with some uncertainty. Show-through from the reverse page appears faintly in the right margin and is left out. A faint library stamp at the lower left is left out.
